title: For the noobs using HTML
author: Moist_Signal_5080
selftext:
This is me, I’m a noob using strictly a single HTML file. All my development is done in the Claude browser (or app), by staring a new session after every task and uploading my HTML directly. My file got to the point that is too large and I needed to use a new chat window after every single task. Eventually it got to the point that just uploading the HTML causes Claude to compact the chat, before anything else even happened. This was killing my hourly and weekly limits.

Then I got the $100 Claude Cloud credit the other month. Figured I’d find a way to burn it up so it didn’t expire. So I uploaded my game html and MD file into a private GitHub repository.

Then I realized how much more efficient it was, using significantly less than my old method. While also quicker and easier to start a new session, no longer have to download the html, then re upload it. I just simply select the repo and send a prompt.

The one thing to watch out for (again I’m a noob) is to make sure it’s updating your main file. I had a few sessions where it just did a separate branch and never merged it into the main. So I was working off the old version. Then I had Claude merge them all together, some had overlapped work they did similar things in different ways, but it sorted it easily.

If your working locally on your PC, this might not apply. But I’m running on a garbage laptop and using my phone on the go.

TLDR: using a GitHub repo and Claude code is cheaper to use than straight chat for HTML files.

comments.author: derAres
comments.body: Edit: Editing my old comment to put it more positive: we were all there. We all had a moment where it clicked. welcome. There is still much to be learned. You know who to ask 😊

comments.author: SassyTextDev
comments.body:
I don't 100% understand what you're saying.

You're making a game, and you're putting everything (structure, styles, scripts) into a single HTML file, and you've got a git repo for just that file, and you initiate claude... on the repo?

I'd love to check it out and offer up some advice. I'm confident I could suggest a better workflow. Something you could paste into claude oc. Private DM me the repo?

replies.author: Moist_Signal_5080
replies.body:
Yes everything is contained in the single file, it’s built with html5/JS. You can open the single html in a browser and the full game is there, no external assets. I know a lot of people that never coded or made a game, found out that “Claude can make a game for you”. When you come in with this approach, it seems the quickest and easiest route is for Claude to start building an html file right there for you.

So now I have a private repo, give Claude full access to it, then I can select it in the “Claude code” tab. When Claude to work on it, it goes straight to the repo and makes a branch to edit. This is significantly less token consuming than what I was doing.

replies.author: SassyTextDev
replies.body:
Dang, alright man. Well look, I don't mean to come off condescending, but I've absolutely been there before. Shit man, I started my career when HTML5 was just released. I've made the single file index.html canvas games. Back in notepad++. In a cave with a bucket of bolts.

At the start it fast as fuck, because everything is just **there**. But as you add complexity to the ~~project~~ *file*, it's going to start to chug.

Do this for me. Get yourself a folder. Slap that file in it, start claude in the folder and say this.

>Hey Claude, listen. We've been building this single-file project for a while now, and you're starting to chug, so we're going to set up a workflow here.

>I need you to look at the project and understand what we built, and then write yourself an [agents.md](http://agents.md) file so that every fresh Claude has a summary of what this is. Then I need you to break this file out. Nothing fancy, but at least put the code in a couple of TypeScript folders. At least put the styles somewhere. If you want to get SCSS, that's fine. If you want to do Tailwind, that's fine. At least break up the HTML with components. If you want to do React, that's fine. If you want to do something less costly and more lightweight, that's fine too.

>Write in the [agents.md](http://agents.md), say that the owner/operator of this project isn't extremely computer savvy and so will often start a conversation without having run \`npm run start\` or whatever. Hell, he may never know what that even means. If you find yourself struggling with something, you are absolutely authorized to reorganize and cut stuff out and trim stuff down.

>If you want to write a real quick test while you're developing, for the sake of scaffolding, that's great, but don't go too crazy with the tests. If you want to use the Chrome Dev Tools MCP to launch it in a browser and try the game yourself, go ahead and do it. You're the only cowboy coder in this project. No one else is looking at the code, so this is your domain.

>If something sucks in terms of "sucks to work in," you're the only one that can decide to fix it, so just go ahead and fix it on the fly. Work in branches. Once the owner's happy with a branch, merge it in and push it up.

>Until we hear otherwise, we don't need crazy version control. We don't need egregious amounts of tests. We don't need 10:1 comment-to-code ratios. We just need to get shit done for fun.

>Capture all this in the [agents.md](http://agents.md) file, and then do a quick "figure out everything that's going on" and split everything out into reasonable libraries. Make sure that the next agent through also knows that it can do that.

  
Run this in a folder claude has 100% auth on, and every subsequent conversation should take place in that folder. I'd say Iterm2 or something, but you're probably more comfortable with the claude chat. That's fine.

Also, please god please install \`chrome-devtools-mcp\`. Just... ask claude to install it and then "yes" to everything. It's WAY more efficient than the *chrome plugin*. Think of it like this. The chrome plugin is "take a snapshot of the page, click an area". Claude reading an image is maybe 2K tokens. BIG. DevTools is "give me the rendered HTML, and let me run scripts inside the window, and let me drive the browser". Way more abilities, way less tokens.

comments.author: Zestyclose_Day4993
comments.body:
As you are spending money on a claude subscription I could recommend you to pay for a vps in some cheap host like contabo or hetzner. 
Then using termux on your phone you connect to the vps using ssh and launch claude code there. By that way you can use claude code from your phone into a real computer. Also in that vps you can link your github account to save the changes in your repository

comments.author: shaymagen
comments.body: Same thing clicked for me. once it's in a repo it only reads what it needs instead of the whole file every time. next thing that helped was splitting the html into a few js files so small edits stop touching everything

comments.author: seventyfivepupmstr
